description.short: A cross-platform offline-first application utilizing a custom synchronization queue for network resilience, featuring real-time shared counters and native deep linking integration.

long.label: Project and Experience
long.text: Tally is a cross-platform counter app for personal and shared tracking. Users can update counters immediately, invite participants through deep links, and continue working through poor connectivity.

long.label: System Design
long.text: Actions update local state first and enter a durable command queue. The API, database, and real-time layer coordinate replay and synchronization across reconnects, restarts, and concurrent devices.

long.label: Decisions and Tradeoffs
long.text: Offline support shaped authentication, idempotency, state reconciliation, and web/native token delivery. I accepted additional coordination logic to keep the interface responsive and recoverable.

description.short: A reaction-time training app with timed drills, animated feedback, user accounts, and performance history, backed by a secure Express/PostgreSQL API.

long.label: Project and Experience
long.text: Reaction is a training app built around configurable reaction-time drills. Players can adjust each drill, receive animated feedback, and review results across recent sessions and their full profile history.

long.label: System Design
long.text: Vue and Pinia manage the game flow while GSAP coordinates feedback and transitions between game states. An Express and PostgreSQL API stores accounts, results, statistics, and the settings used for each attempt.

long.label: Decisions and Tradeoffs
long.text: Saving a settings snapshot with every result preserves the context behind historical scores and makes filtered comparisons reliable. Cookie-based authentication and rate limiting protect the account flow without adding friction to each drill.

description.short: A real-time tic-tac-toe lobby with JWT-authenticated Socket.IO sessions, server-side move validation, rematches, forfeits, and disconnect recovery.

long.label: Project and Experience
long.text: GameLobby turns tic-tac-toe into a complete multiplayer flow with authenticated lobbies, live matches, rematches, forfeits, and recovery from temporary disconnects.

long.label: System Design
long.text: Socket.IO connects each player to a server-authoritative game session that validates moves, turns, and match outcomes. User-to-socket tracking supports reconnects and multiple tabs, while Prisma and PostgreSQL persist users and games.

long.label: Decisions and Tradeoffs
long.text: Keeping match rules on the server prevents clients from creating conflicting game states. Soft-disconnect handling adds session complexity, but it avoids ending a match whenever a connection briefly drops.

description.short: An algorithm visualization prototype featuring an insertion-sort visualizer using Pinia and GSAP for playback, scrubbing, animation settings, and synchronized explanatory text.

long.label: Project and Experience
long.text: AlgoVisualizer explores how interactive animation can make algorithm steps easier to follow. The insertion-sort module supports playback, scrubbing, speed controls, and explanations synchronized with each visual change.

long.label: System Design
long.text: A Nuxt and Vue shell provides category navigation, search, and dynamic visualization modules. Pinia coordinates interface state while a GSAP timeline acts as the playback engine for animation and explanatory text.

long.label: Decisions and Tradeoffs
long.text: The playback timeline stays outside Vue's reactive system because it is an animation controller rather than interface data. This keeps state updates predictable while preserving precise control over navigation and timing.

description.short: A TypeScript CLI for packaging, installing, and running LangGraph workflow templates with manifest-based distribution and bundled OpenCode execution assets.

long.label: Project and Experience
long.text: MAWM is a CLI for packaging, installing, and running reusable LangGraph workflow templates. It gives projects a consistent way to add planning assets, start workflows, resume threads, and review results.

long.label: System Design
long.text: Typed commands and validated metadata drive manifest-based install, update, removal, and listing flows. Installed templates combine scaffolded LangGraph packages with OpenCode assets that manage local servers and workflow run state.

long.label: Decisions and Tradeoffs
long.text: Global template installs encourage reuse, while project-local assets preserve the context needed for each codebase. Bundling the execution assets increases package scope, but removes repeated setup from every workflow.
